source.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
source.authors: Xin-Long Zhao; Dong-Sheng Liu; Heng-Yu Zhao; Zi-Xuan Fu; Zheng Wang; Jie Cai; Jie Zhou; Qian Ma; Xuan-He Zhou; Xu Han; Yu-Dong Wang; Zhi-Yuan Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training-token budgets and measures downstream benchmark performance, a different measure from held-out cross-entropy or fitted scaling-law prediction.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out cross-entropy, sweep parameter count or compute, fit power laws, or test extrapolation from small runs. Its relevant results are downstream benchmark scores across token budgets on FineWeb; the paper gives explicit aggregate scores at 16B and 20B tokens and reports additional token-budget curves.
record.test_reason: This is a data-refinement paper. Kaplan et al. is cited only as motivation in the introduction. The 'token-budget' results are intermediate checkpoints (4–20B tokens) of single 21B-token cosine-schedule runs at one model size (1.36B). They are used to compare UltraX against Raw and ProX-C data. The study measures no held-out loss, fits no power law, sweeps no parameter count or compute, and does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or loss. Its results therefore do not bear on any version, including V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that UltraX gives the highest average downstream score on all five corpora (≈2.0% and 1.53% relative gains over Raw and ProX-C). They also conclude it matches or beats the baselines with fewer training tokens on FineWeb, showing better data efficiency and refinement reliability. They make no claim about scaling laws themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The study refines pretraining data and evaluates downstream benchmark scores; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law measurements of held-out loss, parameter count, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with corpus and refinement method; the paper reports that Raw and ProX-C gains become relatively saturated in later FineWeb training, while UltraX performs better earlier.

fits_no_version.finding: Within single 1.36B runs on FineWeb, average downstream score rises with consumed tokens (Raw 39.8→45.1, UltraX 40.2→46.1 over 4–20B). Raw and ProX-C gains are described as saturating late. UltraX reaches 45.49 at 16B, above the baselines' 20B scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data refinement shifts the downstream-accuracy-vs-tokens curve, improving token efficiency at fixed model size.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The relevant evidence uses downstream benchmark scores rather than held-out cross-entropy and covers only one reported model size. No uncertainty estimates or prediction tests are reported for the token-budget results.
record.rows_left_out: The paper includes per-benchmark results and token-budget curves for multiple corpora and methods (Figure 2, Figure 4, Tables 15–19). They are not extracted here because the relevant version is downstream predictability and the reported evidence does not fit or evaluate predictions; the explicit aggregate FineWeb results described in the text are retained.

untested.parts: Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss. Only checkpoint scores within single runs at one model size are reported, with no fit or prediction.
All: no loss measurements or power-law fits.
All: no extrapolation from small runs.
All: text pretraining only, no fitted law.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V6 'limits_scope' label are not justified. The checkpoint curves are a data-efficiency comparison inside cosine-schedule runs, with no scale or loss predictor. The scaling-law reference appears only in the abstract and introduction as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test prediction from pretraining loss, fit a predictive relation, or vary model parameter count; the token-budget analysis is on FineWeb with a fixed model size.

rows.subject: MiniCPM (UltraX, FineWeb)
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-token budget and measured average downstream benchmark score.
rows.baseline: Raw and ProX-C at 20B tokens: 45.08 and 45.05
rows.note: The text says this 16B result exceeds the 20B final scores of Raw and ProX-C.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with baselines: UltraX at 16B tokens vs Raw/ProX-C at 20B. The 16B value is an intermediate checkpoint of a cosine-decay run, not a separate budget, and no predictive relation is fitted. It measures data efficiency, not downstream predictability.
